01 / 04

Understanding the customer side of a business

My profile records completion of Sales Fundamentals for Entrepreneurs, issued by LinkedIn in July 2026.

Sales Operations is the associated skill. The course sits alongside my business administration, finance, and resilience learning, giving another angle on how an organisation turns an idea into something people will choose to use.

The connection

For my current interest in corporate and commercial law, understanding a business should include understanding its customers.

Read the deeper context+

A product may be technically impressive, but the commercial question is how it meets a need and how that value is communicated. This is introductory learning, not a claim that I have managed a sales team or built a company.

02 / 04

Questions I want to investigate

I want to become better at asking what a business offers, who it is intended for, and why someone would choose it.

Those questions can make a company announcement more useful to analyse. They shift attention from the excitement around a product to the assumptions on which its adoption depends.

The connection

My reflections on technology events provide a starting point for that habit.

Read the deeper context+

Demonstrations show a capability; the harder question is what makes it practical in a real setting. Sales learning adds a customer perspective to that question, alongside the operational and technical perspectives I have encountered elsewhere.

03 / 04

A practical next step

A useful exercise would be to examine a public product launch and write a short account of the customer need, the proposed value, and the open questions.

That would be a learning exercise rather than a professional market assessment, but it would make the course context more concrete.

The connection

The next stage is to support an interpretation with evidence, distinguish a company’s claims from what has been demonstrated, and explain the reasoning clearly.

Read the deeper context+

Those are habits I want to develop across my commercial reading, rather than treating a certificate as the end of the subject.
